## Objective

Adapt canonical AffineMap[Fixed,Moving,D3] to the existing supplied initializer behind the HalfFlow boundary. Feed the exact inverse of Flashalign movingToFixed; qualify frame/layout/direction and midpoint split prerequisites without importing halfflow.internal into consumers.

## Source and ownership

PRD: `docs/plans/flashalign-implementation-prd.md` (version 2, SHA-256 `a66500fec106a0df0f6635bb81329f44cca0a031cab32958c6c370f2ca6fc929`). Relevant sections/work packages: 3.2, FA-14A. Original proposal and Python oracles are in `docs/plans/flashalign/` and `docs/plans/flashalign-prd.md`.

Planned paths (reserve exact paths at implementation time):
- `HalfFlow-owned affine input adapter`
- `endpoint/midpoint adapter tests`

## Acceptance criteria

1. Landmark and asymmetric-grid tests prove direction and no initializer double composition.
2. Valid affine with unsupported midpoint split produces typed failure rather than invented matrix roots.
3. Default HalfFlow initializer/objective remains unchanged; same input transforms retain parity on JVM/JS.

## Blocking prerequisites

- L18 (`bd-01M2B116QF782AWRSZBGMGXKMR`): FA-L18: Implement typed linear result records and canonical output
- C02 (`bd-01M2B119YT1YVJ9SWD6X4Z38RG`): FA-C02: Qualify a frozen HalfFlow/BasinBridge comparison baseline

## Evidence and completion

Record exact candidate/provider hashes, relevant commands and outcomes, fixture/config identities, numerical tolerances and all failure cases. Run the task-specific independent checks above and affected JVM/Scala.js/consumer gates; keep timing and scientific accuracy claims separate. Missing required input or a failing admission gate remains blocked, not silently passed. A completed experiment may report no benefit; dependent release/adoption milestones must still assess their own criteria.

## Integration constraints

Use canonical image4s/Ravel/Gale and existing reframe4s map/resample/registration ownership, typed failures and immutable plans with explicit workspaces. Preserve strict compiler policy, current motion/HalfFlow defaults, dirty-tree ownership and frozen experiments. Keep Flashalign linear execution free of nonlinear setup and direct HalfFlow dependencies. Shared primitives migrate through their current owner with both-consumer evidence; do not merge method objectives.
